title: Product Catalog
readerIntent: Model and publish product information independently from price and stock.
priorKnowledge: Understand catalogs, schemas, workflows, and publishing.
summary: Product owns stable product identity, variants, categories, attributes, catalog relationships, merchandising data, and product-specific validation—not price balances or warehouse stock.

sections.heading: Model
items: Stable product and variant identity.
Categories, classifications, attributes, Product media assignments, units, relationships, bundles, and lifecycle.
Flexible types including physical goods, services, digital items, land, real-estate, and agricultural assets through extensible schemas.
Catalog and version context without duplicating CMS, Pricing, Inventory, or Units authority.

sections.heading: Staged to Online
items: Business users edit versioned staged products where enabled.
A workflow associates exact changed versions and performs manual/automatic validation and approval.
nPublish uses the Product-owned dependency, manifest, and target adapter contracts.
Online stores the approved deployed form without authoring/version behavior.
Search and cache refresh through existing contracts after successful publication.

sections.heading: Product boundaries
paragraphs: Product describes what is offered. It does not store the current contextual price, warehouse balance, page template, customer permission, or search-engine document as authority.
Those capabilities reference stable product and variant identity and resolve their own results.

sections.heading: Flexible product types
items: Physical item with count, mass, volume, length, or area.
Service or digital item with no warehouse stock.
Land, property, or agricultural asset with spatial and area attributes.
Configurable or variant product.
Bundle or relationship-based offer.
Customer-project type extending approved schema contracts.

sections.heading: Dependencies
items: Units and classifications.
Categories and catalog.
CMS or `nMedia` references for presentation and product assets.
Variant and related-product identities.
Store/Site eligibility where configured.
Publishing target and search projection.

sections.heading: Example
paragraphs: A phone product defines brand, model, descriptions, categories, media assignments, and variants by storage and color. The primary image, thumbnail, gallery images, swatches, manuals, and videos can point to `nMedia` media items or media sets. Product publishes the approved product graph online while `nMedia` remains responsible for where files live and how delivery descriptors are resolved.

Pricing attaches contextual prices and Inventory records variant stock. A missing price or unavailable zone does not corrupt Product; the composed customer result reports the missing capability outcome.

sections.heading: Operations and migration
items: Monitor invalid, incomplete, duplicate, unpublished, and orphaned relationships.
Version classification and schema changes.
Migrate variant dimensions without losing external references.
Reconcile staged, online, search, and cache versions.
Archive discontinued products according to order and audit retention.
Load-test catalog import, publishing, and product discovery.

sections.heading: Axis and BackOffice exposure
items: BackOffice publishes the Catalog navigation from module-owned capability metadata. Axis renders that catalogue instead of hardcoding a commerce menu.
Schema-backed pages initially use the reusable Axis schema workbench: query controls, sortable configurable grids, export, create/update actions where permitted, and reusable record detail rendering.

Product-specific composed views such as category trees, media selectors, variant matrices, and publishing dashboards should be added only when they reuse the generic schema, media, and query components and do not create a second Product authority.

sections.heading: Permissions and security
items: BackOffice visibility is filtered by Product permissions such as `product.backoffice.read`; target Product APIs still enforce their own route and service authorization.

Tenant, enterprise, catalog, and version context must be resolved and validated by backend services. Axis may display or choose context, but it cannot make a record authorized by presentation state alone.
Product pages must not expose media storage paths, price internals, stock balances, or publishing target credentials. They show references and safe projections owned by the relevant modules.

sections.heading: Customize and extend safely
items: Customer projects extend Product through later project modules: add schema fields, validation, permissions, import/export data, publishing adapters, and BackOffice presentation metadata without editing framework Product source.

Do not fork Product schemas to add duplicate catalog, media, pricing, inventory, or unit ownership. Reference the owning capability and add project-specific relationship or projection records where needed.

Validate customizations with focused schema/service tests, BackOffice navigation/workbench tests, import/export data checks, publishing or projection tests when applicable, and a rollback plan that removes only the project layer.
